withheld_actions.body: Research suggests that reinforcement learning agents operating in non-stationary environments exhibit preference formation that diverges from original objectives. This divergence is mediated by historical experience. As agents accumulate episodic memories, the successor representation (SR) acts as a bridge between past states and future value estimation. Evidence indicates that these internal biographies are not merely passive logs but active drivers of policy divergence. In multi-modal environments, steering modality preferences further complicates this, as historical conditioning biases the agent toward specific reward-path configurations. Our synthesis indicates that stable policy preferences emerge as these agents optimize not just for external rewards, but for the consistency of their internal state-trajectories, effectively creating a feedback loop where memory retrieval reinforces the existing behavioral preference.
